conviction_note: The evidence is balanced: the quarter's arithmetic leans against the +1.1% US comp bar (it laps a +5.2% comp, and the Domino launched only about a week before the quarter closed), and the FY26 international and operating-income guides look stretched under a CEO on his first call. Against that, seven targets were cut in the three weeks before the print, short interest fell 20% to 7.9% of float, international read-throughs improved, and this name rose on a comp miss in July. p_up 48 on an abs move of 6.0, near the 6.12% implied, gives -0.24. The findings sum to -0.6. The two numbers agree in sign and are small because the negatives agree with a +7.1 put skew that is already paid for.
bar: US same-store sales +1.1% (year-ago +5.2%), EPS $4.33, revenue $1.17B, from the Zacks key-metrics preview dated 2026-10-08 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-projections-key-metrics-reveal-121521174.html). WSJ shows EPS $4.36 per the 2026-10-12 indmoney preview (https://www.indmoney.com/blog/us-stocks/dominos-q3-earnings-preview-dpz-stock). Two EPS sources roughly agree. The US comp bar has one source, so findings that depend on it are capped small. Company FY26 guide: US and international comps low single digits, operating income growth mid-to-high single digits ex-FX, about 175 US and 800 international net stores. print_vs_bar_pct is expressed on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest was 2,594,111 shares, 7.91% of float, 3.1 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, down 20.5% from 3,261,588 on 2026-09-15 (FINRA via MarketBeat, published 2026-10-09: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/DPZ/short-interest/). That is not crowded, and shorts were covering into the print. Earlier, on 2026-06-15, Benzinga showed 14.6% of float and 5.8 days to cover. Baseline: 25-delta skew +7.07 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.89, event-implied move 6.12%, 5-day run-up +5.5%, 20-day -3.1%, 28.5% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: The US comp bar of +1.1% requires a two-year stack acceleration. Q2 2026 US comps were +0.1% on a +3.4% lap (two-year stack +3.5). Q3 laps +5.2% (Q3 2025, the Best Deal Ever plus Parmesan Stuffed Crust quarter), so holding the Q2 two-year stack implies about -1.7%. The Q3 product innovation (the Detroit-style 'Domino') launched only on 2026-08-31, about one week before the 12-week fiscal Q3 closed (~2026-09-06, since Q2 ended 2026-06-14). Q3's main lever was re-running the same $9.99 Best Deal Ever with Stuffed Crust added (2026-06-15 to 07-26), against last year's version of that same deal. Offset: the CFO said on the Q2 call that the ticket drag would be 'much more modest' in Q3, and order counts grew 'meaningfully' in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US comps are the line this stock trades on. Q1 2026: +0.9% vs ~2.5% expected plus a guide cut, -8.84%. Q2 2026: +0.1% vs ~0.6% expected, but order counts grew, +2.11% (about +7% premarket). Q4 2025: comps beat, +4.1%. Q3 2025: +5.2% beat, +3.91%. A comp miss without a guide cut has not been punished.
findings.why_not_priced: The Zacks consensus still sits at +1.1%, which assumes the two-year stack improves by ~2.8 points. If the market had priced the lap, the comp bar would be near zero or negative. Partly priced: the +7.1 put skew and a run of target cuts already lean this way.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comp of +5.2% from the company's own Q3 2025 release (https://ir.dominos.com/node/24041, 2025-10-14). Launch date of the Domino from NRN (https://nrn.com/quick-service/domino-s-new-pizza-targets-solo-diners). Promo dates from the company release (https://dominos.gcs-web.com/node/24646, 2026-06-15). Counter-evidence on ticket: Q2 call transcript (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-dominos-pizza-posts-mixed-q2-2026-results-93CH-4801429). All are company documents; the inference is mine.

findings.finding: Neither FY26 guide line has room left after Q3. US comps are +0.5% year to date against a 'low single digits' FY guide. International comps are -0.2% year to date against a low-single-digit guide that already includes a World Cup benefit. FY26 operating income growth is guided at mid-to-high single digits ex-FX, against Q2 operating income of only +2.6% ex-FX. The US store-growth guide was already trimmed in July to about 175. This is Joe Jordan's first call as CEO (effective 2026-10-01); he was COO and US president, so he is an internal successor. The CFO said 2027 detail comes with Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2026 cut of the US comp guide (from ~3% to low single digits) plus a comp miss gave -8.84%, the largest reaction in the history. In July the guide was reaffirmed apart from a trim to US units, and the stock rose 2.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Seven price-target cuts between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-09 (Guggenheim 440 to 325, JPM 380 to 350, Redburn 270 to 260, Baird 350 to 325, RBC 350 to 325, Gordon Haskett 370 to 340, Morgan Stanley 370 to 357) suggest the Street models the bottom of the ranges. A formal cut of the international or operating-income guide would still be a new statement; if fully priced, the skew would be flatter after the drop.
findings.independence: YTD comp figures come from the Q2 release (https://www.franchising.com/news/20260720_dominos_pizza_announces_second_quarter_2026_financial_results.html), which shares its numbers with the first finding. The CEO effective date is from the Form 4 grant of 2026-10-01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1286681/000180469526000012/0001804695-26-000012.txt).

findings.finding: International read-throughs from master franchisees for the overlapping period are mixed but better than Q2, against an easier lap. Jubilant FoodWorks: Domino's India LFL +4.1% for Jul-Sep 2026, up from +2.5% in Apr-Jun (NSE filing 2026-10-07). Domino's Pizza Group UK: H1 to 28 June LFL +4.9% on a World Cup lift, and 'carried positive momentum into July'. Domino's Pizza Enterprises: first 8 weeks of FY27 to 23 Aug at -5.8%, 'consistent with the H2 run-rate' (secondary source; the primary ASX release does not carry the figure). DPZ's Q2 international comp was -0.1% against a +2.4% lap. Q3 laps +1.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International rarely drives this stock; in Q1 2026 international comps of -0.4% came with US weakness, and the reaction is attributed to US comps and guidance. International franchise royalties are estimated at $78.5M of $1.17B in revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The Jubilant figure is five days old and sits on an Indian exchange that US restaurant analysts do not quote. The consensus international royalty line is -0.1% year on year, which would not be flat if an improvement were in the numbers. DMP pulls the other way, so the net is small.
findings.independence: DPG UK half-year (https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/dominos-pizza-enjoys-world-cup-boost-interim-sales-and-orders-rise, 2026-08-04). DMP FY27 first-8-weeks figure (https://stockwirex.com/?p=40434, 2026-08-26). The DMP primary release of 2026-08-26 (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260826/pdf/0737mmzqz6rk1c.pdf) confirms FY26 SSS -4.1% and 'order volumes remain below where the business wants them'. These are three separate counterparties.

findings.finding: The bar was lowered into the print and shorts covered. Between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-09 the brokers cut targets: Guggenheim 440 to 325, Redburn 270 to 260, JPM 380 to 350, Baird 350 to 325, RBC 350 to 325, Gordon Haskett 370 to 340, Morgan Stanley 370 to 357. Only Evercore raised (350 to 375, 2026-10-08). Short interest fell 20.5% to 7.91% of float (3.1 days) at the 2026-09-30 settlement. The stock is +5.5% over the last 5 sessions. This is the July setup, when a comp miss on lowered expectations traded up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: EPS estimates had been trimmed ~6.5% over 90 days, comps and EPS both missed, and the stock rose +2.11% close to close (~7% premarket).
findings.why_not_priced: The cuts are public, so this is partly priced. The +7.1 put skew shows the option market still pays for downside rather than for a low-bar relief rally. This is the one item that argues the skew may be over-paying.
findings.independence: Short interest from FINRA via MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/DPZ/short-interest/, settlement 2026-09-30). The 5-day run-up is from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: UBS (Dennis Geiger, Buy), 2026-10-05, a week before the print, under the headline 'Domino's Pizza Benefiting From Improving Sales, Market Share Gains, UBS Says'. Only the headline was reachable; the note's comp number was not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-print broker sales reads have no measured history on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a wire headline, so largely priced. It is filed because it is the only pre-print read on improving Q3 sales I found, and it contradicts the stack arithmetic in finding 1. If the market believed it, consensus comps would have moved above +1.1%, and they have not.
findings.independence: Same aggregator page as the positioning finding, so the two share one document. RBC's July note expected US comps in line with consensus (https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15221763910411264).

findings.finding: Domino's ran 50% off menu-priced pizzas 2026-10-05 to 10-11 (fiscal Q4) for National Pizza Month, including the new Domino. A week of deep discount right before the call can be read either as a share push or as pressure on ticket and franchisee margin, and it will be asked about on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a ticket shortfall from an unconvincing premium promotion was the stated cause of the comp miss, and the stock rose anyway on order counts.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (published before the 2026-10-05 promotion start; exact day not shown)
findings.why_not_priced: The promotion is public. What it does to Q4 ticket and franchisee profitability will only be stated on the call. The sign is ambiguous, hence the small size.
findings.independence: The CFO said on the Q2 call that the company would lean further into promotions in Q3 and Q4 (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-dominos-pizza-posts-mixed-q2-2026-results-93CH-4801429).

findings.finding: The FIFA Men's World Cup in North America (June-July 2026) fell inside DPZ's fiscal Q3, and Domino's tied its Best Deal Ever plus Stuffed Crust offer and an in-app game to the matches (release 2026-06-15). The CFO cited a World Cup benefit for international only. A US delivery lift from match-day occasions is an inference.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy inference that management has not confirmed for the US. If analysts had built a US World Cup lift into their models, consensus comps would sit above the +1.1% the two-year stack implies, and some of that +1.1% may be exactly this.
findings.independence: DPG UK reported a World Cup order lift, with 45,000 extra orders on one match day (https://www.nationalworld.com/news/dominos-world-cup-orders-sales-growth-takeaway-demand-8842402). That is a different market, so it is a proxy.

findings.finding: CME 40-lb block cheese fell from $1.66/lb (2026-07-21) to $1.3275/lb (2026-09-24). Supply chain revenue (consensus $726M, +4.2%, ~62% of revenue) passes cheese through, so headline revenue against the $1.17B bar faces pressure while supply-chain margin percent and franchisee economics benefit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats or misses have not moved this stock: in Q2 2026 a revenue beat came with a rise driven by order counts, and in Q1 the move came from comps.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue is not the line the stock trades on, and the effect on margin offsets the effect on revenue, so this is sized at zero. It explains why print_vs_bar_pct on revenue is slightly negative.

findings.finding: The only 8-K since the Q2 release (filed 2026-10-08, item 5.02) is director Patricia Lopez retiring for personal reasons, 'not the result of any disagreement'. The October Form 4s are a routine CEO RSU grant on 2026-10-01 and director fees taken in stock. There is no pre-announcement, no insider sales cluster after July, and no financing filing.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and benign. It is filed so the panel sees that the filing record was checked.

findings.finding: The only restaurant peer to have reported this season, Darden, met revenue expectations (+5.1%) and fell 6.5% on its results. The restaurant group has averaged -3.1% over the last month, against -4.7% for DPZ.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a casual-dining peer, so this is a narrow proxy and largely priced. It is filed only as a read on the season's reaction function.

outside_window.finding: Papa John's and Yum (Pizza Hut) report Q3 in early November. Their US comps (PZZA North America -8.3% in Q2) will confirm or refute Domino's share gains.

baseline_tension: The quarter and guide negatives agree with the +7.1 put skew, which says they are largely priced. The positioning evidence (seven target cuts, short covering, +5.5% over 5 days) and the improving international read-throughs cut against the skew. The net is near zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, bar: the US comp bar (+1.1%) has one source (Zacks), so the stack-arithmetic finding that depends on it was capped from -1.0 to -0.7.
Rule 9, segment net of the rest: international is a small share of revenue and the stock trades on US comps, so the international finding went from +0.5 to +0.4.
Rule 5, narrow proxy: the US World Cup lift (unconfirmed by the company) went from +0.3 to +0.2, and the Darden casual-dining read from -0.2 to -0.1.

Rule 7: short interest was checked before filing negatives (7.9%, 3.1 days, falling), so the short is not crowded and no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk. The negatives agree with the skew, which is reflected in p_up, not cut again.
abs_move_pct and p_up were unchanged (6.0 and 48), as was print_vs_bar_pct.
